newsitem.title: MACEDONIA: World Bank says Macedonia has turned corner.
newsitem.headline: World Bank says Macedonia has turned corner.

text.p: The World Bank said Macedonia had made good progress with political and economic reforms and welcomed a decision by the European Union to give $50 million in aid to the former Yugoslav republic.

The European Commission is expected to announce during the Bosnia Donors' conference in Brussels this week that the EU is willing to grant Macedonia a loan of 40 million ecu to help it with its balance of payments.
The Ecofin council supported a proposal at a meeting in Brussels last week, presented by EU Commissioner for Monetary Affairs Yves-Thibault de Silguy, for macro-financial aid to Macedonia.
"Macedonia should warmly receive the Ecofin decision," head of the World bank mission in Macedonia Ellen Goldstein said.
"As a result of this announcement many pieces of a large puzzle can come together and provide Macedonia with financing in the order of $130 to $150 million."

A World Bank source in Macedonia said part of the country's balance of payments gap could be filled by potential donations and loans from the World Bank, International Monetary Fund and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development.

Goldstein said: "The World Bank is very satisfied with the cooperation of the current Macedonian government and hopes to see five percent growth of real GDP in Macedonia in each of the next three years."

Since 1994 Macedonia has received $270 million from the World Bank, $160 million was given in the form of balance of payment support linked to economic reforms and restructuring and $110 million was for investment in transportation, agriculture and the private sector, the bank said.
"It is clear that Macedonia has turned the corner of what has been a period of economic decline inevitable since the political change that has occurred since the late eighties," said Goldstein.
"Macedonia has stabilised this decline and has experienced modest growth in 1996. We are assuming and hoping that this trend will continue and that the government can pursue its reform programme."
